title: SUBTOTAL: one function number, six answers

docs.syntax: =SUBTOTAL(function-number, range) with 9 (or 109) for SUM, 4 for MAX, 5 for MIN, 2 for COUNT
docs.explain:
SUBTOTAL opens with a number instead of a range. That number chooses which of the built-in functions runs: 9 adds, 1 averages, 2 counts, 4 takes the largest. The range follows it. On this sheet =SUBTOTAL(9,B2:B4) adds the three prices to 35, and the second screen swaps in 4 for a maximum of 20.

The number exists for filtered lists. A filter hides rows, a plain SUM keeps adding them, and a SUBTOTAL recalculates against the rows that remain. Numbers from 101 to 111 go further and skip rows hidden by hand, so 9 and 109 agree here only because nothing is hidden.

Both screens point at the same three cells, so the first argument is the only difference between them, and it moves the answer from 35 to 20. Read that number before the range: it decides whether the range is being added or searched for its largest value.

errors.text: The first argument is missing or is not one of the numbers SUBTOTAL recognises, so nothing says what to calculate.
The range was deleted, so the reference no longer points at any cells.
The number says COUNT or MAX while the question asked for a sum, and the answer measures something else.

docs.atWork: The total row under a table that gets filtered during a review meeting.
docs.outcome: Read the function number first, so one range can be added or searched for its largest value.
docs.teaches: SUBTOTAL's function number choosing SUM, MAX and COUNT over the same range
docs.dataset: Stock list with a total row that needs a subtotal

screens.prompt: In D5, add up the prices with SUBTOTAL rather than SUM.

hints.syntax: =SUBTOTAL(9,B2:B4): the number comes first, then the range.
hints.func-subtotal: Nine is the SUM inside SUBTOTAL, which is what the total row of a filtered table needs.
hints.require-ref: The range is the price column of the table.
hints.value: Ten plus five plus twenty is 35.
hints.error: The total is being divided by zero, which turns it into #DIV/0!.

reject.why: a plain SUM keeps adding rows a filter has hidden
the last price is left out of the range
function number two counts the rows instead of adding them
the range starts one row late
the total is divided by zero
the range sits outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In D5, find the largest price in the table with SUBTOTAL.

hints.syntax: =SUBTOTAL(4,B2:B4): four is MAX, and the range follows it.
hints.func-subtotal: MAX is not called by name here: the number in front of the range selects it.
hints.value: The largest of ten, five and twenty is 20.
hints.error: The answer is then divided by zero, so the cell returns #DIV/0!.

reject.why: the largest value is right, but the question asks for SUBTOTAL
five is MIN, so the smallest price comes back
nine adds the column instead of finding its largest value
the range stops before the largest price
the quantities are read instead of the prices
the number and the range are not separated
the answer is then divided by zero

seo.title: SUBTOTAL in Excel: one function, six answers
seo.description: The first argument of SUBTOTAL is a number, and that number picks the function: 9 for SUM, 1 for AVERAGE, 2 for COUNT, 4 for MAX. Read it before the range.
